messages:
Ana: Heads up — observed ~8-12% p99 regression on hosted after the kernel-autotune push last night for sequences around 1k-1.5k tokens. Root cause still fuzzy.
Sam: Which path is showing the regression, prefill or decode?
Ana: Mostly the prefill->decode handoff. Prefill stayed on kernel_A (packed GEMM), decode switches to kernel_B (kv-optimized) above a threshold. Autotuner bumped the threshold to 1024 at 02:14 UTC.
perf-bot: Profiling summary (run=1767834000): prefill/kernel_A = 120ms, decode/kernel_B = 95ms, handoff memcpy = 40ms, KV cache miss_rate=14% :eyes:
Kevin: 14% KV miss is worrying. Are we evicting KV segments during handoff or doing extra allocations?
Jess: I also noticed autotuner reduced the batching window for long sequences — more small batches slipping through. That increases scheduling overhead.
Ana: Important detail: kernel_B expects contiguous KV layout. Our handoff inserts a memcpy that fragments the buffers. That could explain the extra 30-50ms.
Sam: Can we adjust autotuner to use effective_seq_len (after trimming pad) rather than raw token count? That would avoid bumping mid-roll for padded sequences.
perf-bot: Current autotune config snippet:
```
buckets:
  - max_tokens: 512
    kernel: kernel_small
  - max_tokens: 1024
    kernel: kernel_medium
  - max_tokens: 2048
    kernel: kernel_kv_tiled
kv_layout: contiguous_required: true
autotune: enabled: true
thresholds: [512, 1024, 2048]
```
Sam: Action plan: 1) Kevin run microbench with thresholds {1024,1280,1536,2048} 2) Jess prototype prefill padding-trim + contiguous KV rewrite 3) Ana prepare rollback PR for autotune threshold to 1536.
Kevin: Running now on perf cluster (4 runs each). Preliminary numbers: 1024 -> +9% p99, 1280 -> +5%, 1536 -> +1%, 2048 -> ~0% change. Uploading traces to s3://redwood-perf/176783/
Maria: Can we do a quick config rollback to 1536 in prod while we stabilize? Customers on dedicated plans saw a few requests spike.
Ana: Yes I will open a config PR to set threshold back to 1536 and disable the aggressive kernel flip.
Jess: I'll try trimming padding before the bucket decision so sequences with lots of trailing pad don't get misclassified. Will bench on the same harness.
Sam: Also check batching policy — if autotuner shrank the window we should revert that for longctx to avoid small-batch penalties.
perf-bot: Logged: rollback-requested by Ana. Ticket INF-4271 created.
Kevin: Uploaded perf traces + flamegraphs: s3://redwood-perf/176783/flamegraphs.tar.gz. Early look shows memcpy at handoff + scheduling stalls.
Ana: Thanks. If 1536 shows safe behavior we'll rollout rollback config in next 15m. I'll post status here when done. :thumbsup:
Maria: I'll prepare a short customer note saying we observed a perf regression and are reverting an autotune change; ETA 30m.
Sam: I'll coordinate with oncall for the rollback window.
Jess: If rollback stabilizes, we should add an autotune integration test that fuzzes padding and verifies kernel switches don't add >3% p99 overhead.
Ana: Agreed. Adding test to the perf harness item.
perf-bot: Reminder: add regression label to the autotune PR and link INF-4271.
